text:
maria: heads-up — saw a KV miss storm on the last canary deploy, ~3x p95 for small requests. attaching quick notes.
aj: ugh noted. same cluster? any autoscaler activity around that time?
maria: yes same cluster, we had an autoscale-up event at +30s into the deploy. p95 spike lines up with pod churn and lots of cold kv loads.
tez: do we know if kernel selection or batching heuristics made it worse? iirc the new kernel patch changes prefetch behavior.
maria: profiling points to higher per-token kernel latency for short sequences on that build. also batching was suboptimal — requests got spread into many small batches during the scale-up.
sam: sounds like a classic cold-cache + small-batch combo. we should try deploy-time warmers + a coordinated schedule for the autoscaler window.
ben: agree. propose two quick mitigations: 1) run deploy-warmers that hit hot prefixes right after each rollout, 2) temporarily force larger batch-window (200ms) during scale events.
anya: for (1) we should be careful not to overload GPU memory with kv priming. can we limit key cardinality per warmer job?
maria: warmer job plan: run 30s after deploy on each node, synthetic traffic with top-100 prefixes only, rate-limited to 50 rps per node, and backoff on errors. sample config:
```yaml
warmers:
  delay: 30s
  prefixes: top_100
  rps_per_node: 50
  concurrency: 4
  kv_limit: 2000
```
ci-bot: deploy started: canary-2022.11 -> nodes=6->9 at 2022-11-15T18:42:01Z :rocket:
maria: also testing a hybrid approach: scheduled prefill jobs that run every 15m during high-traffic hours to keep KV hit-rate > 80%, plus deploy warmers for immediate priming.
aj: how do we pick keys? static top-100 will drift. we need a TTLed popularity list from the console metrics.
tez: we can compute rolling hot prefixes from request logs, expose as /hot-prefixes endpoint for warmers to consume.
sam: alternative: use a light-weight sampler in the autoscaler hook to inject sampled real requests as warmers during scale-up — less synthetic and more representative.
ben: note on regressions — kernel change that reduced L2 prefetch gave -5% overall throughput but +12% throughput for long seqs. We need rollout gating per workload profile.
maria: agree. action items:
- tez: add /hot-prefixes endpoint (rolling 30m window)
- aj: add CI test that simulates autoscale + deploy churn and measures KV hit-rate and p95
- sam: prototype autoscaler hook that replays sampled real requests to new pods
- ben: prepare rollback plan if kernel patch raises short-sequence latency > 15%
anya: timeline?
tez: can have endpoint by EOD tomorrow. aj can add CI sim early next week. sam will prototype this week.
maria: cool. I'll schedule a dry-run on staging at 09:00 UTC tomorrow with warmers + adjusted batch-window. ping me if you want to join. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: scheduled job created: staging-warmers-2022-11-16T09:00Z (id=warm-2212345)
ci-bot: note — monitoring alert will mute for 10m during scheduled dry-run to avoid noise.
maria: thanks all — logging this thread and will paste run results after the dry-run.
